newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria defers ruling on troubled Dobrudzha bank.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria defers ruling on troubled Dobrudzha bank.

text.p: A Bulgarian court on Tuesday delayed ruling on an insolvency suit against private Dobrudzha bank for seven weeks after experts declined to prepare reports on its financial state, the national radio said.
"Two of the three experts appointed by the court said they declined to make reports on the bank's financial state. The Dobrich court postponed ruling on the case for April 29," the radio said.
Ruling was previously postponed in December when the court appointed experts to ascertain the bank's assets-to-liabilities ratio as of the moment when the central bank sought its insolvency.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) put Dobrich-based Dobrudzha bank in receivership on September 23 and filed an insolvency suit against it on October 31.
The BNB said that the bank had a minus 54.06 percent capital-to-risk assets ratio as of August 31, 1996 and 588 million levs of outstanding payments as of September 20.
The BNB has opened bankruptcy procedures against 15 state and private banks or a third of Bulgaria's banks since May last year.
Only one of them, Madan-based private Crystalbank, has been declared insolvent by the court so far.
Court rulings are expected on state-owned Mineralbank, Private Agricultural and Investment Bank and private Trade and Savings Bank by end-March.

Under plegdes made to the International Monetary Fund Bulgaria is expected to adopt a new Bank Insolvency Law to speed up liquidation of insolvent financial institutions. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
